decisions.executionNote: Begin symmetric gradual wrist reorientation with clearance; monitor IK continuity and gripper geometry.
Pitch grippers to downward approach while moving toward left car and right chocolate bar; keep elbow-up continuity.
Align open jaws with left car and nearer right chocolate bar, descending conservatively toward grasp height.
Finish short downward approach and close both grippers around the car and chocolate bar; verify retention with a subsequent lift.
Large descent residual suggests contact rather than a secured grasp. Reopen, rise, and correct lateral alignment using both camera views.
Replan rejected recovery with an initial near-hold and smaller lift increments, then adjust open grippers toward object centers.
Use wrist views to center each object's narrow dimension within the jaws; approach from slightly above the previous contact height.
Apply small center corrections, close both jaws, and test retention by lifting four centimeters.
Transport visibly retained car to left basket and chocolate bar to right basket, raising to clear basket rims.
Car slipped and remains outside left basket. Hold left open; advance retained right bar with smaller increments and reduced height after continuity rejection.
Release right chocolate over red basket and withdraw slowly from near-extension; reopen left and recover slipped car.
Clear basket edge with partly narrowed left jaws and center the car. Approach the green pepper with right arm; deposited chocolate remains in red basket.
Narrow left jaws to avoid white basket rim, then settle onto car. Center and close right jaws around green pepper; both holding commands zero.
Move left grasp toward car's front to clear the basket obstruction; test green-pepper retention while lifting and moving inward with right.
Clear obstructed left basket rim and restore vertical gripper orientation; reapproach the green pepper at its rolled position.
Center the car and pepper using corrected vertical approaches, close at body height, and pause before checking retention.
Lift both newly centered grasps slowly while holding zero closure targets, checking that objects follow before further transport.
Right pepper is retained: carry toward middle basket. Left car was not retained; reopen and lower farther over its body, avoiding the rim.
Close left at a lower car-body grasp and test a small lift; continue carrying green pepper toward the right half of the middle basket.
Test the lower car grasp with a vertical lift. Recover slipped green pepper at its new location, retreating from the rejected extension before descending.
Reduce initial right retreat increments after zero-step rejection; lift left vertically and approach dropped pepper with open right jaws.
Car now follows the left gripper: carry slowly toward white basket. Regrasp green pepper lower around its center and start a short lift.
Car contacted the basket rim and fell: back off for regrasp. Raise retained pepper well above rim, then tilt forward to reach blue basket without extending the elbow fully.
Both objects are again on table. Recenter more deeply around object bodies; narrow left opening to avoid basket and restore vertical right approach.
Clear left rim and make jaw spread parallel to the basket front; recenter the displaced green pepper from wrist feedback without descending further.
Lower vertically with rim-parallel jaws, close around car and pepper bodies, then make a minimal retention test lift.
Lift vertically above basket rims with a gradual forward pitch to preserve elbow margin; verify objects remain between closed jaws.
Carry the visibly held car above white basket after added rim clearance; recover green pepper from its exposed side without gripping the blue rim.
Move retained car safely inside white basket, release and withdraw. Settle right jaws lower around the pepper belly and test a short lift.
Car is inside white basket. Approach yellow pepper with left; move right jaws farther around green pepper's broad center rather than pinching its end.
Close around centered yellow pepper and test lift; pull right grasp gently away from blue basket before further transport.
Yellow pepper is retained: raise and carry toward middle with forward pitch. Right jaws are obstructed by basket rims; open and withdraw before changing grasp direction.
Carry held yellow pepper over blue basket with forward reach and elbow clearance. Approach green pepper again with narrowed, rim-parallel jaws.
Release yellow pepper over blue basket and withdraw left. Close right around the centered green pepper slightly lower, then make a short vertical retention test.
Yellow pepper is in middle basket. Lift the centered green-pepper grasp clear of rims, and move empty left arm aside for safe separated workspaces.
Green pepper is visibly retained. Carry it above the right half of the middle basket with added rim clearance; keep left safely stationary.
Release green pepper inside blue basket, then withdraw. Stage left arm on its own side while right prepares to collect remaining objects.
Approach the remaining chocolate bar at its right-side end, rotating jaws across its narrow width while keeping right EE on its own side.
Make a small transverse correction around the bar's accessible end, close, then pull gently away from the rim to test retention.
Right end grasp missed. Withdraw right safely; approach the bar's center using left arm in its own workspace for an intermediate tabletop transfer.
Center left on chocolate body with a narrow opening. Independently approach remaining car with right, aligned across its width and keeping arms on their own sides.
Narrow left jaws to clear the rim while centering the chocolate; correct right transverse alignment over car body, close both and test small lifts.
Correct left grasp for the bar's offset from the jaw center. Lift held car with right and rotate it across the center for a separated tabletop handoff.
Open centered left jaws before descending around the thin bar. Place car horizontally at the workspace boundary for later left-arm pickup, without crossing the arms.
Withdraw right after placing car at boundary. Change left to a pitched approach from the front to clear the basket rim obstructing the thin chocolate grasp.
Advance along the pitched approach toward the chocolate body, then close with the basket rim behind the elevated jaw.
The pitched grasp is still above the thin bar. Reopen, lower cautiously while correcting its transverse offset, then close again.
Test the low pitched chocolate grasp with a slow lift and retreat away from the basket, judging retention only from the next views.
Chocolate grasp was not retained. Switch to the car staged at the boundary, approaching its left portion from the left workspace; keep right clear.
Approach the staged car from the left with a small inward pitch and transverse correction, keeping the left EE on its own side and right stationary.
Center the staged car transversely between left jaws, settle slightly lower, close and test a short lift; right remains clear.
The car is centered but the pitched jaws appear above its body. Reopen and lower 25 mm before reclosing, keeping both arms separated.
Test the deeper car grasp with a slow lift and movement into the left workspace, maintaining closed jaws and fixed orientation.
Car now follows the left gripper. Raise and carry toward the white basket, gradually changing to forward pitch while keeping clearance for the hanging car.
Carry the securely held car over the white basket at rim-clearing height, adding forward pitch without approaching full extension.
Correct zero-step tensor rejection: move car farther inside white basket, release, and withdraw with right stationary.
Both cars are now in white basket. Approach the remaining bar's left end with closed vertical jaws to shift it away from the obstructing rim into right-arm reach.
Set the closed left jaws beside the bar's left end and gently slide it rightward while the left EE remains on its side.
Bar shifted into right workspace. Release any left rim contact and withdraw; approach shifted bar with open right jaws from the front.
Clear the obstructing rim and turn right jaws parallel to basket front for an end-to-end bar grasp. Move empty left farther back in its workspace.
Approach the bar with jaws parallel to the rim, spanning its ends instead of placing a finger against the basket wall.
Close the right end-to-end grasp and lift away from the basket rim to check whether the bar follows.
Reopen and bring the bar into the jaw line using a small forward correction before descending further; the previous end grasp missed.
Reposition behind the bar's exposed front edge while lowering the end-spanning jaws, avoiding further approach toward the basket wall.
Reach the thin bar at a lower grasp height with rim-parallel jaws, then close; the wrist view may be occluded by the basket.
Pull the low closed grasp away from the rim while lifting slowly, checking whether the chocolate follows or remains on the table.
The rim still blocks a low grasp. Approach the bar's left end with closed right jaws to slide it out to a clear area before grasping.
Set the closed right fingertips low beside the bar end, then gently slide rightward to move it away from the blue basket obstruction.
The bar is tucked under the basket lip. Pitch the closed, rim-parallel right fingers from the front while retracting the wrist to clear that lip.
Place the pitched closed fingertips beside the bar's left end, then sweep gently rightward and forward into clear tabletop space.
Raise clear and rotate about the pitched gripper approach axis, changing to a narrow-width grasp with the rear finger elevated above the basket lip.
Descend the pitched narrow-width grasp around the bar while keeping the rear jaw clear, then close and pause.
Correct the bar's remaining transverse offset with a narrow opening, close around its body at the pitched low approach, and test a short lift.
The bar remains on the table. Reopen narrowly and settle the pitched fingers lower onto its thin side walls before closing again.
Test the lower side-wall grasp with a slow upward retreat away from the blue rim, keeping right jaws commanded fully closed.
Shift the narrow grasp along the bar to place more of its body between the pads, descending from the clear front side before closing.
Correct the bar's lateral offset into the narrow right jaw opening and settle lower around its sidewalls before closing.
